text:
Recent work supports combining sequential prediction with item graphs, while separating similarity from complementarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary products as relevant yet functionally dissimilar, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters. [SAGERec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/24/4844) combines a global semantic graph with a lightweight Transformer, but uses LLM-derived representations, incompatible with the no-pretrained-weights constraint. [STAR (CIKM 2024)](https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/245900224/3627673.3679999.pdf) demonstrates interpretable sparse term matching, but its BERT-based architecture and user-review inputs also prevent direct adoption here.

A constraint-compatible research hypothesis: retain SASRec; add a small, directed graph of transitions observed exclusively in training histories and a separate title/description similarity branch. Encode text using local TF–IDF word/character features with a learned projection, or randomly initialized token embeddings pooled and trained jointly with next-item prediction. Keep graph neighborhoods sparse and learn a residual gate so content associations cannot dominate sequence evidence. These are proposed adaptations, not published performance guarantees; compare sequence-only, graph-only additions, text-only additions and their combination using macro validation HR@10.

Treat transition edges as behavioral associations and lexical similarity as content overlap: neither establishes substitutes, complements or physical compatibility. Reserve explicit compatibility claims for available descriptions that name a supported model, connector or standard; generic shared terminology remains uncertain. Preserve separate evidence channels and retain original model identifiers during tokenization. Learn all representations from permitted data, without review text, relation labels from external datasets or pretrained weights.
